text: Track 2.1 Today, Yuyan and Liang are going to talk to us about traditional festivals in China. And there are a lot of them. Isn't that right, Yuyan? Yes, because Chinese culture is a very ancient culture. We have a long history and a lot of festivals. Some are thousands of years old. There are two types of festival – local ones, which people celebrate in certain areas of the country, and national festivals, which everyone celebrates. We're going to talk about the big national festivals. And Liang's going to begin with the Spring Festival. Yes, the Spring Festival is the biggest holiday in China. Everyone takes at least a week's holiday from work, and we all go home to our families. The festival celebrates the Chinese New Year, and it takes place at the end of January. The traditional festival lasted a month. Now, most people only celebrate Chinese New Year's Day itself and the day before it. On the day before, we clean everything in our houses, and we decorate everything with the colour red, a lucky colour in China. We prepare special dishes for the evening when people celebrate by eating a big dinner with their family and giving each other gifts. Children get new clothes and gifts of money in red envelopes. There are lots of fireworks to welcome the New Year. On New Year's Day, people go out in the streets to meet their friends, and there are parades with traditional entertainment, such as lion dancing, with people dressed up in amazing traditional lion costumes. The next festival we are going to talk about is the Mid-Autumn Festival. This takes place near the beginning of October, and it celebrates the moon. It's another festival where families usually get together. The special dish for the festival is mooncakes, which people give each other as gifts. Making mooncakes is very important, and every family has their own way to do it. Families usually celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival with a big dinner. One favourite activity is going outside to look at the moon. Parents tell their children traditional stories about it. In some parts of China, parents try to find wives and husbands for their sons and daughters.
